findings.reason: The protected Python solution uses two deques (one for enter state 0, one for exit state 1) and simulates second-by-second door crossing while skipping empty time gaps. It maintains previous_direction (defaulting to 1/exit when idle). The event-driven queue simulation runs in O(n) time and O(n) space; no candidate is required.

When both queues have waiting people, the direction used in the previous second is prioritized. If that queue is empty, the other direction crosses. Idle gaps fast-forward current time to arrival[next_person] and reset previous_direction to 1 (exit). Non-decreasing arrival order ensures FIFO deques preserve index-order priority.

Each person is enqueued and dequeued exactly once, and empty gaps fast-forward directly, yielding O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space for the deques and answer array. Complexity evidence is inherited and hash-bound.
Accepts arrival and state lists, returning an array of exact crossing times for each person in index order.

The approach accurately details two-queue FIFO state tracking, door priority logic (previous direction / default exit), time gap fast-forwarding, and O(n) time / O(n) space bounds. Alternatives and edge cases cover unsorted list searches, second-by-second walking, idle second resets, same-second arrivals, same-direction index ties, empty preferred queues, and continuous backlogs.
